Cost depends on your program and your insurance benefits, so the only real answer comes from a free, confidential benefits check. If you're uninsured or a plan doesn't cover treatment, our team will walk through every option with you — sliding-scale fees, private pay, and financing. Financial barriers shouldn't stand between you and care.

Many of our clients keep working full-time during treatment. Our Evening IOP meets after typical work hours, and treatment records are protected by HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 — we never contact your employer, and verifying benefits doesn't notify them either.

Your privacy is protected by HIPAA and by 42 CFR Part 2, a federal confidentiality law specific to addiction treatment. We never contact your employer, and verifying your insurance benefits doesn't trigger any notification to them.

Getting started is one phone call: our team confirms your insurance benefits for free, schedules a clinical assessment, and most clients begin treatment the same week. You'll always talk to a real person, never a call center.

Yes — our Virtual IOP and telehealth services serve clients throughout California, with the same clinical team as our in-person programs. It's a real option if distance, work, or family makes commuting to Westwood impractical.

en.a: Detox (detoxification) is the medically supervised process of clearing a substance from the body, usually the first step before treatment when there's physical dependence. Golden State Rehab is an outpatient center and doesn't provide detox on-site — if you need it, we refer you to a trusted partner facility and coordinate your transition into our PHP or IOP program once you're medically stable.

en.q: What is the difference between PHP and IOP?
en.a: PHP (Partial Hospitalization) is our most structured outpatient level: about 5 days per week, roughly 6 hours per day. IOP (Intensive Outpatient) meets 3 to 5 days per week for about 3 hours per session, with morning and evening tracks, so many clients keep working. Which one fits depends on your clinical assessment — our team helps you figure that out.

Medication-assisted treatment combines FDA-approved medications with counseling and therapy to support recovery, most often for opioid or alcohol use. Our medication management program is overseen by our psychiatric team. Whether it's right for you is a clinical decision made with a provider — not something a chatbot can judge.

Dual diagnosis (or co-occurring disorders) means experiencing a substance use disorder and a mental health condition — like depression, anxiety, or PTSD — at the same time. Treating both together matters, because each can feed the other. Our programs are built to treat them as one connected picture.

Recovery doesn't end at discharge. Our aftercare and alumni program keeps you connected — ongoing support, community, and a plan for the transition back to everyday life. We help you build that plan before your program ends, not after.

es.a: La desintoxicación es el proceso supervisado médicamente de eliminar una sustancia del cuerpo, normalmente el primer paso cuando hay dependencia física. Golden State Rehab es un centro ambulatorio y no ofrece desintoxicación en el sitio — si la necesita, lo referimos a un centro asociado de confianza y coordinamos su transición a nuestro programa PHP o IOP.

es.q: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre PHP e IOP?
es.a: PHP (Hospitalización Parcial) es nuestro nivel ambulatorio más estructurado: unos 5 días por semana, alrededor de 6 horas al día. IOP (Programa Intensivo Ambulatorio) se reúne de 3 a 5 días por semana, unas 3 horas por sesión, así que muchos clientes siguen trabajando. Cuál le conviene depende de su evaluación clínica — nuestro equipo le ayuda a decidir.

El diagnóstico dual (o trastornos concurrentes) significa tener un trastorno por uso de sustancias y una condición de salud mental — como depresión, ansiedad o TEPT — al mismo tiempo. Tratar ambos juntos importa, porque uno puede alimentar al otro. Nuestros programas los tratan como un solo cuadro conectado.
